claims.value: Toreno gives side B, Venegas and Senra joined on 12 January, about 8,000–9,000 infantry and 1,500 cavalry.
claims.rationale: Joined force before the battle; separate from Infantado’s reserve and from Bodart’s available whole-engagement population. English rendering (ours): "On the 12th Venegas and Senra together counted about 8,000 to 9,000 infantry and 1,500 cavalry."

claims.rationale: Interested French opponent estimate and absent reserve are not summed into the battlefield population. English rendering (ours): "A total of 15,000, with five guns; he hoped for support from his chief, remaining at Cuenca with a reserve of about 8,000."

claims.value: Toreno says Venegas convened a council while receiving no instruction from his chief; the council moved to Uclés to join Senra and await the duke’s orders.
claims.rationale: Local decision and superior authority are distinct; no exact replacement time is established. English rendering (ours): "With circumstances pressing and no instruction from the chief, Venegas convened a council that unanimously chose Uclés, joining Senra and awaiting the duke’s orders."

claims.value: Jourdan places Victor with only part of his corps when he chose an immediate attack.
claims.rationale: The preceding sentence names Victor. A qualitative subset is not a numeric French return. English rendering (ours): "Although he had only part of his corps, the marshal did not delay the attack."

claims.value: Jourdan says Victor chose to attack immediately after Villatte unexpectedly met the Spanish army.
claims.rationale: English rendering (ours): "Although he had only part of his corps, the marshal did not delay the attack."

claims.value: Jourdan says Victor had no news of the Spanish army when Villatte unexpectedly encountered it on the morning of the 13th.
claims.rationale: Retrospective account of information, not a synchronized knowledge clock. English rendering (ours): "Victor, without news of the Spanish army, intended routes toward Huete and Carasola when Villatte unexpectedly met it on the morning of the 13th."

citations.locator: jourdan, printed p. 144, Internet Archive leaf 161; inspected page-image excerpt
citations.quote: Le maréchal Victor, qui n’avait aucune nouvelle de l’armée espagnole, se proposait de diriger ses troupes, partie sur Huete et partie sur Carasola, lorsque, le 13 au matin, la division Villatte se trouva inopinément en présence de cette armée.

claims.value: Toreno describes the Spanish right as isolated heights divided from others by the Bedijar stream.
claims.rationale: The source’s word strong is attributed description, not an invented defensive score. English rendering (ours): "The right was strong, consisting of isolated heights separated from others by the Bedijar stream."
